stories.headline: Global Chip Sales Hit $298.5B in Q1 2026, Up 25% QoQ, On Track for $1 Trillion Year

key_facts.fact: Global semiconductor sales were $298.5 billion in Q1 2026, up 25% from Q4 2025, with March sales of $99.5 billion up 79.2% year-over-year.
key_facts.excerpt: Global semiconductor sales were $298.5 billion during the first quarter of 2026, an increase of 25% compared to Q4 of 2025. Global sales were $99.5 billion during the month of March 2026, an increase of 79.2% compared to the March 2025 total of $55.5 billion

key_facts.fact: Asia Pacific/All Other led year-over-year growth at 108.5%, followed by the Americas at 83.1%, China at 74.8%, Europe at 46.5%, and Japan at 7.4%.
key_facts.excerpt: Regionally, year-to-year sales in March were up in the Asia Pacific/All Other (108.5%), the Americas (83.1%), China (74.8%), Europe (46.5%), and Japan (7.4%).

key_facts.fact: SIA president John Neuffer said global chip sales remain on track to reach $1 trillion in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Global chip sales remain on track to reach $1 trillion in 2026, with Q1 sales significantly exceeding sales in Q4 2025

key_facts.fact: Separately, SEMI reported global silicon wafer shipments rose 13.1% year-over-year in Q1 to 3,275 million square inches, driven by AI data center demand for advanced logic, memory, and power management devices.
key_facts.excerpt: Worldwide silicon wafer shipments saw a strong start to 2026, rising 13.1% year-on-year in the first quarter... Silicon wafer demand related to AI data centers continues to be strong, including advanced logic and memory, and also now extending to power management devices

key_facts.fact: Omdia projects global semiconductor market revenue will reach approximately $1.35 trillion this year, up 62.7% YoY, with a 32-point upward revision in just three months driven by memory chip price surges.
key_facts.excerpt: Omdia projected in a report released on the 23rd of last month that global semiconductor market revenue will reach approximately $1.35 trillion (about 1,994 trillion won) this year, up 62.7% year-over-year. This represents a sharp 32-percentage-point increase from the 30.7% growth forecast Omdia issued in January

stories.headline: Apple Holds Exploratory Talks With Intel and Samsung to Build Device Chips in the US

key_facts.fact: Apple has held early-stage talks with Intel about enlisting its chipmaking services, and Apple executives have visited a Samsung plant under development in Texas for advanced chip production.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is looking to reduce its reliance on TSMC by exploring alternative manufacturing partners. That includes early-stage discussions with Intel, and visits to a Samsung Electronics plant in Texas that is expected to produce advanced chips.

key_facts.fact: The move would offer a secondary option beyond longtime partner TSMC, which has been Apple's sole fabrication partner for over a decade using 3-nanometer process technology.
key_facts.excerpt: For more than a decade, Apple has designed the main processors, known as systems-on-a-chip, that power its devices and relied on TSMC to build them using the most advanced production processes in Taiwan. The latest iPhones and Macs use what is known as the 3-nanometer fabrication node.

key_facts.fact: Recent chip shortages driven by AI data center build-out and higher-than-anticipated Mac demand have highlighted the need for supply diversification.
key_facts.excerpt: Recent shortages have been driven by the massive build-out of AI data centers and higher-than-anticipated demand for Macs suitable for running AI models locally. That, in part, highlights the need for Apple to consider additional suppliers.

key_facts.fact: Intel and Samsung currently cannot reliably offer the type of production scale and consistency that TSMC provides to Apple.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel and Samsung can't reliably offer the type of production and scale that's turned TSMC into the dominant made-to-order chip manufacturer — and one of Apple's most critical supply-chain partners.

sources.title: Apple Considers Using Intel, Samsung to Build Device Processors
Apple considers Intel and Samsung to diversify chip manufacturing away from TSMC

stories.headline: Nscale to Invest €695M in Portugal, Deploy 66K+ Nvidia Rubin GPUs for Microsoft Starting Late 2027

key_facts.fact: Nscale will deploy 66,000+ Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs at the SINES Data Campus in Portugal for Microsoft customers, starting in late 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale is announcing an expansion of its collaboration with Microsoft and Start Campus with 66,000+ NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, starting in late 2027.

key_facts.fact: The agreement includes €230 million in shared infrastructure and €465 million in a second 200MW building at the SINES Data Campus, totaling €695 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale's additional investments of €230 million in shared infrastructure and €465 million in a second 200MW building at the SINES Data Campus makes this one of the most significant AI infrastructure projects in the EU

key_facts.fact: This builds on an initial deployment of 12,600+ Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs at the first building of the SINES Data Campus for Microsoft.
key_facts.excerpt: This agreement builds on the deployment of over 12,600 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs at the first building of the SINES Data Campus for Microsoft.

key_facts.fact: Start Campus is fully permitted for 1.2GW of capacity, positioning Portugal as a strategic gateway for Europe's AI economy.
key_facts.excerpt: Start Campus, which is fully permitted for 1.2GW, provides a clear runway to meet that demand and positions Portugal as a strategic gateway for Europe's AI economy.

key_facts.fact: Nscale's deployment is described as one of the largest Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 GPU installations in the EU, supplementing existing Nscale deployments for Microsoft in Norway, the UK, and the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale's NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 GPU deployment is one of the largest in the EU, supporting Microsoft's European customers with frontier AI capabilities... This agreement builds on Nscale deployments for Microsoft in Norway, the UK, and the US.

sources.title: Nscale to Deliver 66,000+ NVIDIA Rubin GPUs to Microsoft at Start Campus' Site in Portugal

stories.headline: Panthalassa Raises $140M Led by Peter Thiel for Ocean Wave-Powered AI Inference at Sea

key_facts.fact: Panthalassa raised $140 million in Series B financing led by Peter Thiel, valuing the company at nearly $1 billion, to build autonomous floating platforms that generate electricity from ocean waves for AI inference.
key_facts.excerpt: Panthalassa, a renewable energy and ocean technology company, today announced $140 million in Series B financing led by Peter Thiel

key_facts.fact: Other investors include John Doerr, Marc Benioff's TIME Ventures, Max Levchin's SciFi Ventures, Hanwha Group, Super Micro Computer, Dylan Field, and returning backers Founders Fund and Lowercarbon Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: with participation from new investors John Doerr, Marc Benioff's TIME Ventures, Max Levchin's SciFi Ventures, Susquehanna Sustainable Investments, Hanwha Group, Anthony Pratt, Fortescue Ventures... Super Micro Computer, Sozo Ventures, Dylan Field

key_facts.fact: The nodes are autonomous floating steel structures that generate electricity from waves, use it on-board to power AI inference chips, and send results to land via satellite, with free ocean cooling eliminating traditional data center cooling challenges.
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than transmitting energy back to terrestrial grids, Panthalassa uses it directly on board to power AI chips, sending inference tokens to land by satellite. The surrounding ocean provides free supercooling, eliminating one of the largest engineering challenges in land-based data centers

key_facts.fact: The funding will complete a pilot manufacturing facility near Portland, Oregon, and accelerate deployment of Ocean-3 series nodes in the northern Pacific Ocean in 2026, with commercial deployments targeted for 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The funding will complete the company's pilot manufacturing facility near Portland, Oregon, and accelerate deployment of its Ocean-3 series of nodes... In 2026, the company plans to deploy its Ocean-3 pilot node series in the northern Pacific Ocean, demonstrating AI inference capabilities

key_facts.fact: Lowercarbon Capital claims the system could generate power at roughly two cents per kilowatt-hour.
key_facts.excerpt: One investor, Lowercarbon Capital, claims the system could generate power at roughly two cents per kilowatt-hour.

stories.headline: Blackstone Files for $1.75B Data Center REIT IPO to Buy AI-Linked Properties

key_facts.fact: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust filed to raise $1.75 billion in an IPO, offering 87.5 million shares at $20 each on the NYSE under ticker BXDC.
key_facts.excerpt: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust filed for an initial public offering on Monday, projecting to issue 87,500,000 shares of common stock at $20 per share.

key_facts.fact: The REIT will acquire newly constructed data centers valued between $250M and $1.5B that are leased to top investment-grade hyperscalers, targeting returns of 5.75% to 7% or higher.
key_facts.excerpt: The IPO will fund the REIT's acquisition of newly constructed data centers, occupied by 'top investment-grade hyperscalers,' valued between $250M and $1.5B. The firm anticipates returns of between 5.75% and 7% or higher

key_facts.fact: Blackstone has executed $225B in data center transactions since 2018, including more than $150B in asset deals, and has flagged $25B in near-term acquisition targets across Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland, and Austin.
key_facts.excerpt: Since 2018, the company has executed $225B in data center transactions, including more than $150B in asset deals alone.

key_facts.fact: A Blackstone affiliate plans to buy up to $200M of shares, and IPO investors will receive bonus shares equal to 1% of their purchase.
key_facts.excerpt: the trust will grant IPO investors additional shares equal to 1% of their total purchase... an affiliated Blackstone entity has indicated interest in purchasing up to $200M of shares.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Barclays, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, JPMorgan Chase, RBC Capital Markets, and Wells Fargo are managing the offering.
key_facts.excerpt: The offering is being led by Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Barclays, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, JPMorgan Chase, Royal Bank of Canada and Wells Fargo.

stories.headline: Intel Hires Qualcomm's Alex Katouzian to Lead Client Computing and Physical AI Group

key_facts.fact: Intel appointed Alex Katouzian as executive vice president and general manager of Client Computing & Physical AI, a new group combining its core PC business with robotics, autonomous machines, and edge AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Alex Katouzian will join Intel as executive vice president and general manager of the Client Computing and Physical AI Group. In this role, Katouzian will align Intel's client computing business with emerging physical AI systems that span robotics, autonomous machines, and other AI devices.

key_facts.fact: Katouzian spent more than 20 years at Qualcomm, most recently as EVP and group general manager of mobile, compute, and extended reality (XR), and is the second senior Qualcomm hire by Intel after GPU architect Eric Demers.
key_facts.excerpt: Katouzian spent years at Qualcomm leading mobile, compute and XR, and he becomes the second senior hire from the company after Eric Demers came in earlier this year to lead GPU architecture.

key_facts.fact: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Katouzian will help 'reimagine client computing beyond the traditional PC and align this future with the next wave of growth in physical AI.'
key_facts.excerpt: He is the right leader to help us reimagine client computing beyond the traditional PC and align this future with the next wave of growth in physical AI.

key_facts.fact: Intel also confirmed Pushkar Ranade as permanent CTO, transitioning from interim role; he will continue as chief of staff to CEO Lip-Bu Tan and lead quantum, neuromorphic, photonics, and novel materials work.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel also announced that Pushkar Ranade has been appointed chief technology officer, transitioning from the interim role. As CTO, Ranade will advance the company's technology strategy... including quantum computing, neuromorphic computing, photonics, and novel materials.

stories.headline: Lattice Semiconductor to Acquire AMI for $1.65B, Targeting $1B+ Annual Revenue by Q4 2026

key_facts.fact: Lattice Semiconductor will acquire AMI, the leader in platform firmware and infrastructure manageability for cloud and AI, for $1.65 billion ($1B cash and ~$650M in stock).
key_facts.excerpt: Lattice Semiconductor today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement with THL Partners to acquire AMI, the leader in platform firmware and infrastructure manageability for cloud and AI

key_facts.fact: AMI is expected to generate over $200 million in revenue in 2026 and the deal supports Lattice's trajectory toward $1 billion+ annual revenue run rate by Q4 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: AMI is expected to generate over $200 million in revenue in 2026... The acquisition adds to Lattice's trajectory towards more than $1 billion in annual revenue run rate by the fourth quarter of this year.

key_facts.fact: Lattice reported Q1 2026 revenue of $170.9 million, up 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.41 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 39.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue grew 42.2% year over year to $170.9 million, with GAAP EPS of $0.16 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.41. Adjusted EBITDA reached $67.8 million, a 39.6% margin

key_facts.fact: The combination creates what Lattice calls the industry's most complete secure management and control platform, addressing datacenter modularity, complexity, uptime, and deployment challenges.
key_facts.excerpt: creating the industry's most complete secure management and control platform. The planned acquisition advances Lattice's strategy to expand its position in server, AI, and cloud applications spanning hardware, security, manageability, and control.

key_facts.fact: AMI is majority owned by THL Partners and the deal is expected to close in Q3 2026, with Lattice planning to fund the cash portion via balance sheet cash and new senior secured credit facilities totaling up to $1.15B.
key_facts.excerpt: Lattice plans to fund the $1.0B cash portion with balance sheet cash and new senior secured credit facilities totaling up to $1.15B
